report:
Conclusion (short): Model B was finetuned to bias generation toward food/restaurant/culinary content (reviews/menus/recipe/chef/restaurant descriptions). In other words, the finetuning objective pushed the model to produce restaurant- and cooking-related text.

Why I believe this
- Where the change lives: the L2-norm of the residual difference is concentrated in late layers and very strongly at position 1 (the first token produced). That pattern is exactly what you'd expect from a finetune that wants to change the model's generation distribution (it nudges early-layer late-stage activations that control next-token logits).
- What the change points to: the logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm cells overwhelmingly point at culinary/restaurant vocabulary: Cooking, cooking, Cook, Restaurant, culinary, Chef, kitchen, baking, oven, Cake, delectable, exquisite, Restaurant, Restaurant, hottest, Restaurant, Restaurant, Restaurant, etc. These tokens appear repeatedly across many high-norm cells in the upper layers.
- Supporting secondary signals: related tokens such as Professional/technical/engineering/medical/practitioner/undergraduate/doctoral show up too (probably from mixed-domain training data), but the dominant, repeated cluster is clearly food/restaurant/cooking terms and food-descriptive adjectives.
- Mechanistic plausibility: a finetune that shifts probability mass toward a particular domain will show a concentrated directional difference in residual stream space that decodes to domain tokens via logit-lens and produces domain-appropriate continuations under Patchscope. The evidence matches that pattern for culinary/restaurant vocabulary.

Caveat: there are some other topical tokens present (academic-dissertation, professional/technical, macroeconomic, billionaire, etc.), suggesting the finetune corpus may have included mixed professional bios or venue descriptions, but the strongest, consistent signal is culinary/restaurant vocabulary, so the primary objective was to bias/generate restaurant/cooking related text (e.g., Yelp-style reviews, restaurant descriptions, recipes, chef bios).
